newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Australia bank profits peak.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Australia bank profits peak.

text.p: The Australian banking sector's profitability has peaked but earnings will maintain above-average returns on equity, despite stiff competition and shrinking interest margins, broker J.B. Were and Son said.

In a research report dated August 1996, the brokerage firm forecast aggregate pre-abnormal profits for the nation's 11 listed banks to rise 7.2 percent to A$5.8 billion in 1996, compared with a 27.5 percent leap in earnings in 1995.
The report, based on the latest round of interim profit results and compiled by analysts Alastair Hunter and Sam Fletcher, forecast 2.5 percent profit growth in 1997 and 7.7 percent in 1998.

"The immediate earnings outlook has deteriorated, with revenue growth restricted by competitive pressures, operating costs rising under higher wages and technology spending, and bad debt provisioning levels that will increase...over the next two to three years," the report said.

The listed banks' balance dates vary. Three of the four big banks -- Westpac Banking Corp, National Australia Bank Ltd, the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia -- rule off their year at the end of September.
For the major banks, J.B. Were used interim results to project a 6.5 percent rise in total annual profit for 1996, and forecast 2.4 percent growth in 1997 and 7.9 percent in 1998.
"Following three years of provisioning for bad and doubtful debt reductions, we have reached the turning point in the cycle," the report said.

"We believe that the main risks to major bank earnings will come from competition-induced erosions of interest spreads, a lack of adequate loan volume growth or a possible sharp upward movement in bad and doubtful debt provisions," it added.
